backstage.headline: Own the journey from asking to getting the work done.
backstage.thesis: OpenAI packages the same research engine as a familiar place to start, a workspace that can carry out substantial work, and infrastructure other companies can build on. The strategic prize is continuity from intent to a useful result. Its product expansion, operating leadership and acquisitions increasingly address the work around the model: context, execution, testing, distribution and deployment. Those layers must earn their coherence; a shared brand does not make them one permission boundary or one reliable system.
backstage.object: A task with context, tools and a reviewable result
backstage.question: Can a useful answer become completed work without losing the evidence or the user's control?
sequence: Establish the task and permitted context
Choose a working environment and tools
Review the evidence before accepting or acting

premises.title: Make existing context produce usable work
premises.body: ChatGPT Work gives a familiar conversation somewhere to go: a brief, spreadsheet, deck or other deliverable. Projects preserve relevant sources and instructions across related work. The important transition is from an answer that sounds complete to an artifact whose claims, omissions and intended use can be checked.

premises.title: Delegate the change and retain the review
premises.body: Codex joins model capability to an environment that can read, edit and test a real project. Worktrees and the review pane let a person inspect the resulting change separately from the agent's account of it. The scarce resource shifts toward a clear task, useful tests and reviewer attention.

premises.title: Let builders assemble the execution path
premises.body: The Responses API exposes tool use as structured events. With a configured MCP server, a proposed call, the application's approval response, the call's result and an error are different records. Developers can build their own product around these primitives, while retaining responsibility for permissions, execution semantics and recovery.

choices.choice: Turn broad consumer familiarity into a work surface
choices.gain: People can carry an existing habit into projects, sources and substantial deliverables, lowering the effort of starting a new kind of work.
choices.cost: A familiar interface can make a speculative draft feel authoritative. Source access, conflicting evidence and responsibility for the final decision still have to be explicit.

choices.choice: Own more of the environment around the model
choices.gain: An execution workspace, review tools and product experimentation can make improvements in the model more useful in practice.
choices.cost: Applications, infrastructure and frontier research run on different clocks. More surfaces also create more integration work, operating cost and opportunities for a good local result to fail in the full workflow.

choices.choice: Sell the application and supply its builders
choices.gain: OpenAI can meet direct users through ChatGPT and Codex while developers embed capabilities in their own products. The April 2026 Microsoft amendment expands its cloud distribution options.
choices.cost: Customers need to judge portability as well as capability. A standard protocol does not standardise every tool's behaviour, and OpenAI can also expand into applications built by its ecosystem.

proof.test: Give the work a real source conflict and a clear audience. Measure whether the finished artifact resolves it accurately and how much correction remains before use.
proof.failure: The output is polished but chooses the wrong source, hides an unresolved decision, or needs the user to reconstruct the evidence.

proof.test: Give Codex a scoped change, a missing edge case and an isolated workspace. Inspect the diff, exercise the failure case, and measure review plus rework alongside implementation time.
proof.failure: Passing tests merely mirror the implementation, unrelated changes travel with the task, or staged code is mistaken for a deployed outcome.

proof.metric: Recoverable actions within the intended authority
proof.test: Inspect a proposed tool call, deny an out-of-scope request and simulate a tool failure after approval. Count completed outcomes and recovery effort, not only successful model responses.
proof.failure: The product treats approval as execution, retries an uncertain side effect blindly, or reports a tool result the external service did not return.

sources.title: ChatGPT Work · current official documentation
sources.supports: Work produces reviewable deliverables using files, plugins and approved tools. Local/cloud selection depends on the available environment; non-coding Codex users can use Work's everyday-work experience. Product mechanics rechecked 12 September 2026.

sources.title: Projects and chats · current official documentation
sources.supports: Chats and Sources sections; project instructions and uploaded/connected context; local projects and filesystem projects have different access semantics. Product mechanics rechecked 12 September 2026.

sources.title: Code review · current official documentation
sources.supports: Review pane scopes, inline comments, staging and reverting. The pane reflects repository state, including changes not made by the agent. Product mechanics rechecked 12 September 2026.

sources.title: Git worktrees · current official documentation
sources.supports: Isolated Git working directories and local/worktree handoff. Isolation is an execution mechanism, not proof that the change is correct. Product mechanics rechecked 12 September 2026.

sources.title: Responses API · MCP and Connectors
sources.supports: Tool discovery, allowed_tools, configurable approvals and mcp_approval_request / mcp_approval_response / mcp_call output items; call arguments, output and errors. The demo inspector is an interpretation of these primitives. Product mechanics rechecked 12 September 2026.

strategy.contrast: ServiceNow begins with accountable work already inside the enterprise. OpenAI begins with a person's intent and tries to assemble the context and tools needed to fulfil it. That makes the starting point unusually broad, while leaving the authority of each connected system important.

flywheel.title: Make each capability improvement easier to put to work.
flywheel.body: Familiar products bring in real tasks. Better environments and feedback expose where capability fails to become useful work. Product and research improvements can then reach those users through the same distribution. This is a strategic interpretation, not a claim that all customer content trains the models.
steps: Improve the model and working system
flywheel.constraint: Usage alone does not prove useful completion or sustainable economics. Review effort, reliability, capacity and the cost of delivering longer tasks constrain the loop.

moments.title: A research mission acquires a capital mechanism
moments.fact: OpenAI starts as a nonprofit in 2015 and creates a controlled for-profit subsidiary in 2019.
moments.consequence: The tension between frontier research costs and the institution funding them predates ChatGPT. The corporate structure is part of the strategy, not merely legal background.

moments.title: The model becomes a place people start
moments.fact: ChatGPT launches as a conversational research preview with explicit limitations.
moments.consequence: A direct consumer relationship gives later capabilities a route to users without requiring every user to become an API customer. Familiarity is a distribution advantage; it is not evidence that every answer is dependable.

moments.title: Application execution becomes its own leadership problem
moments.fact: Fidji Simo's Applications appointment is followed by the Statsig acquisition announcement and Vijaye Raji's planned engineering remit. Current OpenAI material describes Statsig's post-acquisition rollout and experimentation work. The io team merger is confirmed in July; LoveFrom remains independent.
moments.consequence: Experimentation infrastructure and interface design address different gaps between a research advance and a product people can repeatedly use. Neither acquisition is a shortcut to a proven integrated experience.

moments.title: The capital structure changes; nonprofit control remains
moments.fact: The recapitalisation completes. OpenAI Foundation controls OpenAI Group PBC through special governance rights, including appointment of the Group board.
moments.consequence: Conventional equity simplifies the growth mechanism while governance retains a separate mission-bearing institution. Formal control is observable; its effectiveness in a future commercial or safety conflict still has to be demonstrated.

moments.title: A central partner becomes a less exclusive route
moments.fact: The amended Microsoft agreement preserves primary cloud partnership and Azure-first distribution while allowing OpenAI to serve all products across cloud providers and making Microsoft's IP licence non-exclusive.
moments.consequence: The strategy gains distribution flexibility without a clean break from Microsoft. Older accounts describing blanket Azure exclusivity no longer describe these terms.

moments.title: Buy the missing parts around sustained work
moments.fact: Promptfoo and Ona now identify themselves as part of OpenAI. In July, the Deployment Company confirms its acquisition of Tomoro while agreeing a conditional Northslope deal. Astral’s reviewed announcement describes an agreement to join; TBPN is separately described as acquired in April.
moments.consequence: Testing, developer tools, persistent execution, embedded implementation and audience reach address different bottlenecks around sustained work. Ownership and product integration are separate milestones: acquired teams do not automatically become one generally available system.

moments.title: The operating structure changes again
moments.fact: Simo announces a move from full-time leadership to part-time advisory work in July, as reported by WIRED. In August, OpenAI appoints Dali Rajic as CRO and announces Denise Dresser will depart after a transition. Current company material identifies Thibault Sottiaux as Head of Core Products & Platform.
moments.consequence: The 2025 Applications hierarchy is historical. The sharper current question is whether product consolidation and more systematic enterprise execution can turn broad demand into dependable deployment through another leadership transition.

leadership.title: A new operating structure has to make adoption repeatable.
leadership.fact: Sam Altman remains OpenAI CEO. Simo shifted to part-time advisory work in July, according to reporting of her announcement. August brought Dali Rajic’s CRO appointment and Denise Dresser’s announced departure after transition. Current OpenAI material names Thibault Sottiaux Head of Core Products & Platform.
leadership.reading: The 2025 Applications appointment was a move toward dedicated product execution, not a stable endpoint. The current organisational signals point to consolidation around the core products and more repeatable enterprise selling and deployment. The challenge is to connect research advances, usable products and customer implementation while leadership responsibilities change. A reporting-line change alone does not establish successful execution.
leadership.watch: Look for accepted work, reliability and lower review burden across the core products, alongside repeatable customer implementation. Foundation control remains a separate governance fact; its effectiveness when mission and commercial incentives conflict must be demonstrated in practice.

essays.title: The front door must lead somewhere.
essays.standfirst: ChatGPT's familiarity matters most when a person can turn it into a usable result without reconstructing the work elsewhere.
paragraphs: A conversation is an unusually forgiving starting point. A person can arrive with an incomplete brief, an unfamiliar problem or the wrong vocabulary and still begin. ChatGPT's original launch established that interaction. The strategic question now is how much work can finish within the relationship that began there.

ChatGPT Work and Projects give that relationship more structure. Sources and instructions can survive across related tasks; Work can turn them into a file or other deliverable that the user can inspect. This changes what completion means. A compelling paragraph is no longer sufficient when the requested output is a comparison someone will use or a presentation someone must defend.

The opportunity is continuity, but its failure mode is borrowed authority. A project can contain an old brief and a newer signed scope without either becoming true merely because it is attached. A confident artifact can conceal that conflict. The scene therefore asks the reader to inspect the competing sources and correct the deliverable while preserving the unresolved decision. In the follow-up, a support-roster change makes the earlier document stale. The signed scope stays intact while the new readiness gap becomes an explicit launch decision.

The 2025 Applications leadership expansion and Statsig integration fit a shift from demonstration to repeatable use; subsequent leadership changes mean that operating design is still evolving. Product iteration can reveal where people abandon or repair a task, although engagement is an incomplete measure of success. The real test is whether the person leaves with useful work and less verification debt.
essays.test: Give the same task to the system with a conflicting source. Does the final artifact surface the conflict and preserve the decision boundary, or merely become more polished?

essays.title: The environment is part of the product.
essays.standfirst: Codex makes a stronger claim than producing code: a delegated task should come back as a change that can be examined and improved.
paragraphs: A model can suggest a correct-looking patch without establishing that it belongs in this repository. A useful coding agent needs the surrounding project, tools and feedback. Codex's worktree and review surfaces expose that larger unit of work: an isolated attempt, the files it changed and the evidence available to the reviewer.

Isolation makes parallel work manageable; it does not validate the result. The review pane can include changes made by the user or another process, so the reviewer still needs a deliberate scope. Tests can also pass while missing the important failure. In the scene, the retry edge case matters more than the first green status, and the implementation and tests can be reviewed and staged separately. A local commit records the accepted change; it still does not ship it.

Astral’s announced combination and Ona’s arrival make sense at these boundaries. Developer tooling strengthens the path from editing to checking; persistent customer-controlled environments address where longer work can continue. Ona now confirms it is part of OpenAI, while the reviewed Astral announcement establishes an agreement rather than a closing date. These moves map the desired system; they do not prove that every integrated capability is already available.

This changes the economics of attention before it changes the economics of every software team. More generated changes can increase the review queue unless tasks, tests and ownership improve with them. The durable advantage would be a higher proportion of changes accepted with less total correction, not simply a larger volume of agent activity.
essays.test: Count reviewer time, failed assumptions and rework along with implementation time. A patch is progress only when its behaviour survives a check the agent did not write to flatter itself.

essays.title: Intelligence still needs an execution contract.
essays.standfirst: The API makes the action sequence explicit. It does not absolve the builder of knowing what an action means.
paragraphs: OpenAI can supply the place a user works and the primitives a developer uses to build a competing place. That dual position is strategically valuable: capabilities can travel through direct applications or somebody else's workflow. The April 2026 Microsoft amendment adds flexibility to distribution while retaining an important partner relationship.

At the product boundary, the Responses API gives this ambition concrete form. A configured MCP interaction can expose a proposed tool call, a separate approval response, and the external tool's output or error. These distinctions are useful precisely because they stop a fluent account of an action from becoming evidence that it occurred.

The contract still belongs partly to the application. An approval must refer to the actual proposed operation; correcting the amount requires a new proposal. After a timeout, the illustrative inspector uses the provider's operation record to distinguish an existing draft, confirmed non-creation and unresolved evidence. A mismatched record cannot close the loop. This recovery and the provider's operation key are fictional application design, not an exactly-once guarantee supplied by the Responses API. A prepared draft is never represented as money refunded.

Promptfoo’s arrival and the Deployment Company’s acquisition of Tomoro recognise other parts of this problem: testing behaviour and implementing systems inside organisations. Northslope is a further agreed addition, conditional in July’s release. Owning more of the stack may reduce handoffs, but it also concentrates dependencies and expands the integration burden. The promise becomes credible through recoverable execution and useful outcomes, not the number of layers under the same company name.
essays.test: Deny one call and fail another after approval. The application should preserve both distinctions and recover without inventing a result or repeating an uncertain side effect.

watch.title: From broader capability to dependable completion
watch.shipped: Current documentation supports ChatGPT Work deliverables and project context, Codex review/worktree workflows, and structured MCP tool calls through the Responses API. These have different environments and access conditions.
watch.next: Watch whether acquired Promptfoo, Ona and Tomoro capabilities become coherent, available customer workflows. The reviewed Astral and Northslope announcements establish agreements, not their current closing status. September management commentary links research, product reach and compute economics; the test is dependable completion at sustainable cost.
watch.boundary: The scenes use scripted fictional data. They demonstrate the documented mechanics, not live models, real tool execution, universal plan access or benchmark results. Company accounts establish strategic intent; they are not independent proof of returns. The OpenAI examples retain their decisions in this browser session. Source revisions, review and staging rules, business validation and provider reconciliation are teaching scenarios around the documented product mechanics.
